summary: Phase 147L.3 was authorized to perform a strictly bounded contract repair of AESIC-001, addressing only the two Non-Blocking findings Phase 147L.2's independent verification surfaced against the v1.1 repair: (Finding 3.1, Major) stage_1_outcome_ref's embedded content had no defined channel into evaluate_stage_2, since AES's unmodified public interface (AESIC-REQ-007/012) accepted only session/package_id, Session was forbidden from carrying Stage 1's outcome (AESIC-REQ-060), and AES itself is stateless (AESIC-REQ-017); (Finding 3.2, Minor) the canonical pointer index (AESIC-REQ-119 item 2) had no defined tamper-evidence mechanism unlike the AER itself. Finding 3.1 is repaired by introducing Stage1EvaluationResult (AESIC-REQ-122, new) as the new return type of evaluate_stage_1 and as a new, optional stage_1_result parameter on evaluate_stage_2 (AESIC-REQ-007/012, repaired): the caller hands back, verbatim, the same object AES already gave it; AES validates it via a mandatory four-check sequence (structural validity, session binding via the already-frozen Session.session_id, identity binding, decision-template binding -- AESIC-REQ-123, new), refusing via a new Stage1HandoffInvalidError (AESIC-REQ-124, new, closed four-reason taxonomy) on any mismatch with zero side effects, and proceeding with stage_1_outcome_ref absent, never an error, when no stage_1_result is supplied (AESIC-REQ-125, new). AESIC-REQ-128 (new) freezes the complete Stage 2 invocation contract. Finding 3.2 is repaired by adding a pointer_digest field to the canonical pointer's own content (AESIC-REQ-119, repaired) computed via the same compute_record_digest function the AER's own digest already uses, plus a mandatory read-time verification obligation (AESIC-REQ-126, new) cross-checking it against the referenced AER's own self-carried digest before treating any pointer as canonical, raising a new CanonicalPointerCorruptError (AESIC-REQ-127, new) on any mismatch, fail-closed, with recovery an operator-owned action mirroring the existing digest-mismatch disposition. AESIC-001 revised from v1.1 to v1.2: 121 requirement numbers preserved unchanged in identity (a small number text-repaired in place: AESIC-REQ-007, 010, 012, 057, 076, 098, 102, 119), 7 new requirements added (AESIC-REQ-122 through 128), zero renumbered, zero reused. All architectural invariants named in this repair's governing prompt (AES sole orchestrator, Registry/Decision-Template ownership, evaluator purity, disclosure-only semantics, non-gating guarantees, Stage 1 advisory semantics, Stage 2 unconditional supersession, immutable AER history, two-tier compound-key model, replay observational equivalence, zero execution capability) confirmed preserved. Zero amendments required to AEM-001, AEMIC-001, IWC-001, IWPC-001, PEC-001, or CHGR-001 -- the one new cross-contract citation (Session.session_id) reuses an already-frozen, already-populated IWC-001 field for a new purpose, not a new obligation on IWC-001. fast_green 4391/4391 and the 183 authority-evaluation tests all passed unchanged, confirming zero regression; no production, schema, test, or runtime file was touched. Overall Verdict: AESIC-001 v1.2 REPAIRED. Recommends 147L.4 (independent verification of this repair), not itself an authorization.

validation_results.name: phase_147l3_root_cause_analysis
validation_results.result: Finding 3.1's root cause traced to AESIC-REQ-118 (Phase 147L.1) requiring the AER to embed Stage 1's already-computed outcome, while AESIC-REQ-007/012/017/060 (all unmodified by that repair) jointly foreclosed every channel by which that value could reach evaluate_stage_2 from evaluate_stage_1's separate, earlier call. Finding 3.2's root cause traced to AESIC-REQ-119 item 2 (Phase 147L.1) defining the canonical pointer's content with no digest of its own, unlike every other durable record family in this codebase (AESIC-REQ-055).
